reason: E1 directly supports the core premise that high lattice distortion and packing density suppress vacancy-mediated diffusion, but it concerns bulk thin-film barriers, not nanoalloys. E2 describes a simulation method and does not provide evidence for the proposed mechanism, the specific strain values, or the baseline design. The translation to nanoalloys and the quantitative strain range are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: High lattice distortion strain energy and high packing density suppress vacancy formation and hinder atomic movement in multi-component alloys.
The substitutional diffusion of atoms via vacancies is the dominant mechanism for interdiffusion in these alloys.
The effect observed in bulk thin-film barriers (E1) translates to nanoalloys and governs structural/chemical stability at high temperatures.
Lattice distortions in the proposed NbTaHfTiZr nanoalloy are in the moderate range of 0.8–1.2% local strain.
Removing one element from the alloy will reduce lattice distortion and packing density, serving as a valid baseline.
